purpose: The branch below made V1.1.2 and V3.2.2 state honestly that their dangerouslySetInnerHTML absence covers apps/web/lib while 23 render-layer files use it, and that what the condition established was narrower than the requirement asked. Saying so is better than not saying so, and it is not a control - reading 27 call sites once is not a control either. This closes it: every call site in the repository is parsed and its HTML has to come from somewhere this repository has decided is acceptable.
requiredInvariants: An analyser that shrugs is an analyser that approves. A call site whose shape the check cannot classify is a failure, not a pass, and the suite asserts that with a ternary it does not understand.

The question answered is 'could this expression be a request value', from the file it is written in - not 'is this string safe', which no static rule can answer. The record says which of the two it is.
No product source is touched. The 27 call sites were already in shapes this check accepts; nothing was rewritten to make a gate pass, and the matrix is identical against main.

The analyser was widened by evidence rather than by convenience. Its first version rejected PlatformV7StrategicHome.tsx because it only recognised module-level constants, and the code there is a local const holding JSON.stringify of a static object with < escaped - idiomatic and safe. Recognising local consts and literal-argument string chains is a correction to the check, and both are bounded: the recursion stops at depth 3, and a .replace() with a non-literal argument is refused because an argument can introduce content.

Reason text is asserted, not only verdicts. Every tainted name would be caught by the catch-all branch anyway, so tests checking only the verdict passed with the parameter and request-shape branches deleted - and the tool would then have told a reader 'not a module-level constant' about a value that came straight off the request. Two mutations went uncaught until the tests asserted the diagnostic.
acceptance: 27 call sites across 23 files, every one classified: 15 static literals, 5 module constants, 3 allowlisted sanitiser calls, 2 JSON.stringify, 1 static template, 1 local constant. None reads a function parameter, props, params or searchParams; none is unclassifiable.

V1.1.2 and V3.2.2 gain a condition citing the analyser, and their scopedAbsence no longer ends in an admission. Both remain PASS and the matrix is unchanged against main: 129/89/88/39, zero requirements changed.

The new condition is revocable: renaming REQUEST_SHAPED in the analyser drops both V1.1.2 and V3.2.2 to NOT_ASSESSED, and restoring it brings them back. The pattern count was checked to zero before the verdict was read.

verify-dangerous-html-provenance.test.mjs passes 11 of 11, with negative controls for a function parameter, for props and searchParams, for a local const bound to a parameter, for a template interpolating a parameter, for a non-literal replace argument, and for a shape the check cannot classify. Five mutations each fail it.
verify-decision-evidence.mjs passes 332 of 332 and verify-absence-scope.mjs still exits 0.
